name: Pineapple
description: Ananas comosus is the cultivated pineapple, a terrestrial bromeliad native to South America (Brazil, Paraguay). It forms a large rosette of stiff, spiny, sword-like leaves (up to 1 m or more) and produces the familiar edible pineapple fruit. The plant is grown commercially in the tropics; in gardens or large conservatories it needs bright light, warmth, and well-draining soil. Unlike the dwarf variety (A. comosus var. microstachys), the typical pineapple is too large for most terrariums but can be used in large enclosures or as a statement houseplant. Flowers are purple to red, followed by the compound fruit. Prefers full sun to bright indirect light and moderate humidity.
careTips: Bright light to full sun - needs strong light to fruit
Moderate humidity (50-70%); can tolerate lower than many bromeliads
Water when top of soil dries; reduce in winter
Feed during growing season with balanced fertilizer
Propagate from crown (top of fruit), slips, or suckers
Non-toxic but spiny - handle with care
